classification.difficultyReason: Combine midpoint relationships, corresponding-side ratios and Pythagoras, including reversing a ratio to determine the draw-bar position.

content.prompt: An engineer is building a trailer. The tray $BDEG$ of the trailer is 2 metres long and 1.5 metres wide—that is, $BD=2\text{ m}$ and $DE=1.5\text{ m}$. The intervals $AC$ and $AF$ represent the draw-bar of the trailer, where $AC=AF$, $C$ is the midpoint of $BD$ and $F$ is the midpoint of $GE$.

spec.description: Rectangular tray with midpoint C on BD and midpoint F on GE. Equal draw-bar arms AC and AF meet outside the rectangle at A. BG intersects AC at I, the horizontal centreline at J and AF at H. Red dashed auxiliary lines run from C to F and from A to CF. Their intersection is unlabelled and marked perpendicular. All four rectangle corners have right-angle marks.
spec.mathematics: BD=2 m, DE=1.5 m, AC=AF, BC=CD=GF=FE=1 m. The perpendicular bisector of CF passes through A and J. Points B,I,J,H,G occur in that order.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens, construction lines, right-angle marks and vertex labels are visible; no calculated answers are supplied.

children.label: a
children.prompt: As part of the design, $AJ=1$ metre. Find, correct to the nearest millimetre:

answer.worked:
Let $K$ be the intersection of the dashed horizontal line and $CF$. Since $AC=AF$, $AK$ bisects $CF$ at right angles. Thus $CK=0.75\text{ m}$ and $JK=BC=1\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{align*}AK&=1+1=2\text{ m}\\AC^2&=2^2+0.75^2\\AC^2&=\frac{73}{16}\\AC&=\frac{\sqrt{73}}4\text{ m}\\AC&\approx2136\text{ mm}.\end{align*}$$

Let $K$ be the intersection of the dashed lines. Then $CK=0.75\text{ m}$, $AK=2\text{ m}$ and $BJ=0.75\text{ m}$. Triangles $AIJ$ and $ACK$ are similar (AAA: right angles and the common angle at $A$).
$$\begin{align*}\frac{IJ}{0.75}&=\frac12\\IJ&=0.375\text{ m}\\BI&=0.75-0.375\\BI&=0.375\text{ m}\\BI&=375\text{ mm}.\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: The engineer changes the distance of $A$ from $BG$ so that $BI:IJ=7:8$. Find, correct to the nearest millimetre:

answer.worked:
$BJ=\frac{1.5}{2}=0.75\text{ m}$, divided into $7+8=15$ equal parts.
$$\begin{align*}BI&=\frac7{15}\times0.75\\BI&=0.35\text{ m}\\BI&=350\text{ mm}.\end{align*}$$

Let $K$ be the intersection of the dashed lines and let $AJ=x$ metres. Then $CK=0.75\text{ m}$, $JK=1\text{ m}$ and $IJ=\frac8{15}\times0.75=0.4\text{ m}$. Triangles $AIJ$ and $ACK$ are similar (AAA).
$$\begin{align*}\frac{x}{x+1}&=\frac{0.4}{0.75}\\\frac{x}{x+1}&=\frac8{15}\\15x&=8(x+1)\\7x&=8\\x&=\frac87.\end{align*}$$
Thus $AJ=\frac87\text{ m}\approx1143\text{ mm}$.

Let $K$ be the intersection of the dashed lines. Use the exact value $AJ=\frac87\text{ m}$, so $AK=\frac{15}{7}\text{ m}$ and $CK=\frac34\text{ m}$.
$$\begin{align*}AC^2&=\left(\frac{15}{7}\right)^2+\left(\frac34\right)^2\\AC^2&=\frac{4041}{784}\\AC&=\frac{\sqrt{4041}}{28}\text{ m}\\AC&\approx2270\text{ mm}.\end{align*}$$
